full_text_en:
Dazong Group Co., Ltd. and Zong Xijin v. Huaibei Shenghuo Mining Co., Ltd., Huaibei Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Guoyang Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over equity transfer

【Ruling Summary】

Mining rights and equity are two different civil rights. If only the company's equity is transferred without causing a change in the subject of the mining rights, it does not constitute a transfer of mining rights, and the transfer contract does not require approval from the geological and mineral resources authorities. Provided that it does not violate mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, the contract shall be deemed lawful and valid. Where a party that delays performance of its obligations under a valid contract claims a change of circumstances based on changes in national policies during the period of delayed performance, such claim shall not be supported.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 236

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Huaibei Shenghuo Mining Co., Ltd., domiciled at Gurao Town, Liehuo District, Huaibei City, Anhui Province.

Legal representative: Zhang Gongmin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Xu Mei, lawyer at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ze, intern lawyer at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Huaibei Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 401, Building 5, Mengshan Middle Road, Huaibei City, Anhui Province.

Legal representative: Zhang Gongmin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Xiaodong, lawyer at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ze, intern lawyer at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Guoyang Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at the Project Department of Hepan Mingcheng Community, south side of Lexing Road, Guoyang County, Anhui Province.

Legal representative: Zhang Gongmin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Xiaodong, lawyer at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ze, intern lawyer at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Dazong Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dazong Village, Zhangwang Town, Tengzhou City, Shandong Province.

Legal representative: Zong Chengle, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Changhui, lawyer at Shandong Huiyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yu Xiangping, lawyer at Liaoning Jingye Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zong Xijin, male, Han Chinese, residing in Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Changhui, lawyer at Shandong Huiyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yu Xiangping, lawyer at Liaoning Jingye Law Firm.

Appellants Huaibei Shenghuo Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenghuo Mining Company), Huaibei Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaibei Real Estate Company), and Guoyang Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guoyang Real Estate Company), in a dispute over equity transfer with appellees Dazong Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dazong Company) and Zong Xijin, being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2014) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 72 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court, filed an appeal with this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegiate panel and held a public hearing to try the case. The following persons appeared in court: Xu Mei and Wang Ze, agents ad litem for appellant Shenghuo Mining Company; Zhu Xiaodong and Wang Ze, agents ad litem for appellants Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company; and Li Changhui and Yu Xiangping, agents ad litem for appellees Dazong Company and Zong Xijin. The trial of this case has now concluded.

Facts Found by the First Instance Court

On March 24, 2013, with Dazong Company and Zong Xijin as Party A and Shenghuo Mining Company as Party B, the parties entered into an "Equity Transfer Agreement". The contents of the agreement are as follows: Party A lawfully and jointly holds 44% of the equity interests in Suzhou Zongsheng Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Suzhou Zongsheng Company) and Huaibei Zongsheng Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaibei Zongsheng Company) (of which Dazong Group Co., Ltd. holds 40% each, and Zong Xijin holds 4% each). Party B is a shareholder of the two companies and has the lawful right to acquire the equity interests of the two companies transferred by Party A and is willing to accept the transfer. After consultation, the parties reached an agreement as follows:

1. Party A agrees to transfer to Party B all of its 44% equity interests in each of the two companies, with a transfer price of RMB 650,000,000 (six hundred fifty million yuan).

2. Time and method for payment of the equity transfer price:
(1) On or before July 31, 2014, Party B shall pay to Party A the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million.
(2) On or before March 31, 2015, Party B shall pay to Party A the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million.
(3) On or before June 30, 2015, Party B shall pay to Party A the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million.
(4) On or before September 30, 2015, Party B shall pay to Party A the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million.
(5) On or before December 31, 2015, Party B shall pay to Party A the equity transfer price of RMB 250 million.
Both parties agree that the aforesaid equity transfer price shall be paid to Dazong Group Co., Ltd., one of the parties in Party A; the internal distribution of the equity transfer price among Party A shall be handled by Party A itself.

3. Within five business days after the full payment of the equity transfer price under this Agreement, Party A shall transfer its 44% equity interests in each of the two companies to Party B in a single lump sum and assist Party B in completing the industrial and commercial registration modification procedures.

4. Special provisions concerning the assets, items, and other property of the two companies:
(1) Whether the exploration permits or mining permits related to the Qilu Sun coal resources, Zhang Youfang coal resources, and Liang Huayuan coal resources (hereinafter referred to as the three coal resources) owned by the two companies are void, expired, or invalid, Party B shall unconditionally perform all terms of this Agreement.
(2) The various licenses, seals, and certificates related to the two companies shall be jointly managed by the parties. Party A and Party B shall convene a shareholders' meeting of the two companies to discuss the method of joint management. Either party must obtain the other party's consent before using any of the aforesaid items.
(3) Within the payment period stipulated in this Agreement, if Party B contacts a third party to purchase the equity interests of the two companies or the exploration rights or mining rights related to the three coal resources under the name of the two companies, and if the equity transfer price or the price for the transfer of exploration rights or mining rights is not significantly lower than the market price, and Party B agrees that 70% of such equity transfer price or price for the transfer of exploration rights or mining rights shall be used preferentially to pay the portion of the equity transfer price under this Agreement that has not yet been paid by Party B, then Party A must unconditionally cooperate with the work of transferring such rights. The parties and the purchaser of such rights shall negotiate the issue of the purchaser bearing the preliminary costs invested by Party A in the Qilu Sun coal resources.

5. Liability for Breach:
(1) Once this Agreement takes effect, both parties must consciously perform it. Any party in breach shall bear liquidated damages equal to 20% of the total unpaid equity transfer price. In addition, the breaching party shall also bear the breach liabilities set forth in subsections (2) and (3) of this clause.
(2) If Party A breaches any term of this Agreement, Party A shall unconditionally refund all equity transfer price already paid by Party B and shall transfer the shares it holds in the two companies to Party B without compensation.
(3) If Party B breaches any term of this Agreement, Party B shall transfer the shares it holds in the two companies to Party A without compensation and shall not request Party A to refund the equity transfer price already paid by Party B to Party A.

6. With the consensus of both parties, this Agreement may be amended or rescinded. If this Agreement is amended or rescinded after consultation, the parties shall separately enter into an agreement for amendment or rescission. In case of any conflict between any agreement signed by the parties before the signing of this Agreement and this Agreement, this Agreement shall prevail. Any commitments, authorizations, or other documents previously issued by the parties to each other shall be void.

7. Party A shall bear all taxes and levies arising from the equity transfer process. Party B shall bear the fees for industrial and commercial registration modification during the equity transfer process.

8. Any disputes or controversies arising from the performance of this Agreement shall be resolved by the parties through friendly negotiation. If negotiation fails, legal proceedings shall be brought to the court of the locality of Dazong Group Co., Ltd.

9. This Agreement shall take effect upon being signed or sealed by both parties.

10. This Agreement is executed in six counterparts, with each party holding two counterparts. Party A (Dazong Company and Zong Xijin) and Party B (Shenghuo Mining Company) affixed their seals and signatures to the Agreement.

After the agreement was signed, Shenghuo Mining Company was obligated to pay the first installment of the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million on or before July 31, 2014, as stipulated in the agreement, but Shenghuo Mining Company failed to perform the payment on time. On July 31, 2014, Shenghuo Mining Company issued a promissory note to Dazong Company for liquidated damages of RMB 20 million. The promissory note stated: "We hereby owe Dazong Group Co., Ltd. the amount of RMB 20 million. This amount shall be paid in full in a lump sum on or before August 30, 2014. Note: These liquidated damages are the liquidated damages arising from the first installment of the exploration right transfer payment of RMB 100 million made between Dazong Group Co., Ltd. and Huaibei Shenghuo Mining Co., Ltd. on March 24, 2013." On September 5, 9, 11, and 12, 2014, Shenghuo Mining Company made four payments totaling RMB 10 million to Dazong Company as liquidated damages, after which no further payments were made.

The first-instance court further found: On July 28, 2007, Shenghuo Mining Company and Dazong Company entered into a "Cooperative Operation Contract", agreeing to jointly register and establish Huaibei Zongsheng Company. Shenghuo Mining Company would transfer the exploration rights of the three coal resources to Huaibei Zongsheng Company and hold 56% of the company's equity. Dazong Company would undertake the construction investment for the cooperative project according to the mine construction design, including underground works, surface works, and the costs for mining roads, power supply lines, wells, and water supply pipelines. Dazong Company would be responsible for handling the project approval for the cooperative development and operation project and bear the costs for the project feasibility report, mine design, environmental impact assessment, and land acquisition, and would hold 44% of the company's equity. On December 15, 2007, Shenghuo Mining Company and Dazong Company entered into another "Cooperative Operation Contract", stipulating that Shenghuo Mining Company would be responsible for handling the project approval, feasibility report, mine design, and environmental impact assessment for the three coal mines. If difficulties arose, Dazong Company would provide active assistance.

On September 18 and September 30, 2011, Anhui Zhiyuan Science and Technology Consulting Co., Ltd. issued appraisal reports on the exploration rights for the coal fields of the three coal resources, with the appraised value of the three coal resources totaling RMB 3.79 billion. On December 3, 2012, the shareholders' meetings of Huaibei Zongsheng Company and Suzhou Zongsheng Company made resolutions, authorizing Zong Chengle to fully negotiate with Wanbei Mining Group Co., Ltd. regarding the development of the three coal resources, with the development methods including cooperative development through equity or the compensated transfer of all resources of the three coal mines to Wanbei Mining Group Co., Ltd. On March 24, 2013, the shareholders' meetings of Huaibei Zongsheng Company and Suzhou Zongsheng Company made resolutions, changing the authorization to Zhang Quanxi to complete the work of seeking and selecting the transferee of equity interests, evaluation, negotiation, and consultation. On June 28, 2013, in a letter to the Huaibei Municipal People's Government titled "Explanation Letter on the Cooperation Situation", Huaibei Mining (Group) Co., Ltd. indicated that it was cooperatively developing mineral resources with Shenghuo Mining Company and requested the municipal government to provide support for the relevant work.

On October 12, 2014, the "Guiding Opinions of the National Energy Administration on Regulating Total Coal Output and Optimizing Industrial Layout" (Guo Neng Mei Tan [2014] No. 454, hereinafter referred to as the Guiding Opinions) was issued. Section 3 of the Guiding Opinions, "Optimizing the Layout of New Construction Projects", requires that, in accordance with the overall requirement of "controlling the east, stabilizing the central region, and developing the west", the development pattern of the coal industry shall be determined based on factors such as coal resource endowment, market location, and environmental capacity. For a period of time in the future, new coal mine projects shall in principle not be constructed in the eastern region.

The first-instance court also found: On October 31, 2014, Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company issued a letter of commitment, stating: "The amounts owed under the equity transfer agreement signed between Dazong Group Co., Ltd. and Huaibei Shenghuo Mining Co., Ltd. on March 24, 2013, shall be performed in accordance with the specific contents and amounts stipulated in the original contract. Huaibei Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Guoyang Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. hereby commit: proceeds from real estate sales shall first be used to repay the due claims of Dazong Group Co., Ltd. in accordance with the contract. This commitment is hereby made."

Shenghuo Mining Company was established on January 12, 2001, with capital contributions from four persons including Zhang Gongmin and Zhang Haiyan. Huaibei Real Estate Company was established on June 26, 2006, with capital contributions from Zhang Gongmin and Zhang Jie. Guoyang Real Estate Company was established on April 24, 2014, with capital contributions from Shenghuo Mining Company. Dazong Company claimed that the three companies were interrelated and that their legal personalities were confused, but upon request by the first-instance court, Dazong Company failed to submit evidence of confusion among the three companies within the time limit.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the equity transfer agreement, the promissory note for liquidated damages, payment vouchers for liquidated damages, the letter of commitment, the cooperative operation contracts, the Guiding Opinions, and the trial transcripts.

Dazong Company and Zong Xijin instituted an action before the first-instance court, requesting: (1) an order that Shenghuo Mining Company pay the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million and liquidated damages of RMB 10 million; (2) that Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company bear joint and several liability for the above debts; and (3) that the litigation costs be borne by Shenghuo Mining Company.

The first-instance court held that the issues in dispute in this case were: (1) whether the doctrine of change of circumstances is applicable to this case and whether the agreement should be rescinded; (2) the validity of the equity transfer agreement at issue and whether the agreement can be further performed; (3) the liability of Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company if the agreement is further performed.

Regarding issue (1), i.e., whether this case constitutes a change of circumstances, the court held: Article 26 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "After the formation of a contract, if there occurs a major change in the objective circumstances that could not have been foreseen by the parties at the time of contracting, and such change is not caused by force majeure nor constitutes a commercial risk, and if the continued performance of the contract would be obviously unfair to one party or would frustrate the purpose of the contract, and the party requests the people's court to modify or rescind the contract, the people's court shall, in accordance with the principle of fairness and in light of the actual circumstances of the case, determine whether to modify or rescind the contract." The term "circumstances" refers to objective conditions, generally meaning all objective facts related to the contract. "Change" refers to an unusual alteration of the environment or basis on which the contract depended. In confirming a change of circumstances, care must be taken to correctly distinguish it from a commercial risk, which requires analysis from the perspectives of foreseeability, attribution, and consequences, based on the case facts. In this case, Huaibei Zongsheng Company was established in 2007, and the applications for mining rights or project approval for the three coal resources at issue had been pursued until the issuance of the Guiding Opinions on October 12, 2014, without having been approved. Furthermore, the Guiding Opinions merely provided that, for a period of time in the future, new coal mine projects would in principle not be constructed in the eastern region. Therefore, the policy factor was not the sole reason for the failure to obtain project approval for the cooperative development project. Additionally, as the two parties had established a company through cooperation, they should share benefits and risks. After the transfer of the company's equity, the transfer price should be distributed according to the shareholders' equity ratios. In this case, Shenghuo Mining Company acquired the equity interests held by Dazong Company and Zong Xijin in the cooperative company in advance. This practice itself carried the commercial risk that a future transfer might not be possible, a risk that Shenghuo Mining Company should have been able to foresee. Moreover, Article 4 of the Equity Transfer Agreement signed in March 2013 also stipulated that Shenghuo Mining Company would unconditionally perform all terms of the Agreement regardless of whether the exploration permits or mining permits related to the three coal resources owned by the two companies were void, expired, or invalid. In summary, it can be determined that Shenghuo Mining Company was able to foresee the possible risks. Additionally, considering that the first installment of the equity transfer price claimed by Dazong Company became due before the Guiding Opinions were issued, it can be confirmed that the doctrine of change of circumstances is not applicable to that installment of the equity transfer price. Therefore, Shenghuo Mining Company's defense of rescinding the contract based on change of circumstances should not be accepted. As for whether Dazong Company had made capital contributions by withdrawal from Huaibei Zongsheng Company, this does not affect the purpose of the equity transfer contract in this case. Therefore, Shenghuo Mining Company's defense for rescinding the contract on the ground that the subject matter does not meet quality requirements should also not be accepted. If Dazong Company had made capital contributions by withdrawal, Huaibei Zongsheng Company had the right to demand that the shareholders replenish the capital contributions.

Regarding issue (2), the validity of the equity transfer agreement at issue and whether the agreement can be further performed, the court held: The Equity Transfer Agreement signed on March 24, 2013, between Dazong Company, Zong Xijin, and Shenghuo Mining Company represented the true intention of the parties and did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, the agreement should be deemed lawful and valid. The equity transfer agreement signed by the parties stipulated that Dazong Company and Zong Xijin would transfer all of their 44% equity interests in Suzhou Zongsheng Company and Huaibei Zongsheng Company to Shenghuo Mining Company, and Shenghuo Mining Company would pay the transfer price. Thus, the parties were in a legal relationship of equity transfer. Shenghuo Mining Company's assertion that this case involved a transfer of exploration rights and that the contract had not taken effect due to lack of approval should not be supported. Further, according to the agreement, Shenghuo Mining Company was to pay to Dazong Company and Zong Xijin the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million on or before July 31, 2014. However, Shenghuo Mining Company failed to fulfill that payment obligation. On July 31, 2014, Shenghuo Mining Company issued a promissory note to Dazong Company for liquidated damages of RMB 20 million and, on September 5, 9, 11, and 12, 2014, made four payments totaling RMB 10 million as liquidated damages. Since the equity transfer agreement is lawful and valid, Dazong Company's and Zong Xijin's claim for Shenghuo Mining Company to continue performance and pay the due equity transfer price of RMB 100 million and the unpaid liquidated damages of RMB 10 million should be supported. Furthermore, Shenghuo Mining Company's defense that it should no longer continue to perform the agreement and that the liability for breach stipulated in the agreement should apply is not tenable because Dazong Company's and Zong Xijin's claim in this case is for continued performance of the original agreement. Therefore, Shenghuo Mining Company's defense should not be accepted.

Regarding issue (3), what liability Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company should bear, the court held: In this case, Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company issued a "Letter of Commitment" to Dazong Company, promising that proceeds from real estate sales would first be used to repay Dazong Company's due claims in accordance with the contract and affixed their seals in the guarantee section. The court held that this letter of commitment represented the true intention of Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company. Their commitment did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and they should fulfill their corresponding obligations in accordance with the commitment. Dazong Company's claim for Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company to bear joint and several liability lacked legal basis. However, Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company should bear joint repayment liability for Shenghuo Mining Company's debts within the scope of the proceeds from the sale of their real estate properties.

In conclusion, in accordance with Articles 44, 60, and 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 64 and 132 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the first-instance court rendered the following judgment:

1. Shenghuo Mining Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay to Dazong Company and Zong Xijin the equity transfer price of RMB 100 million and liquidated damages of RMB 10 million;

2. Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company shall bear joint repayment liability for the above debts within the scope of the proceeds from the sale of their real estate properties;

3. The other claims of Dazong Company and Zong Xijin are dismissed.

If payment of monetary obligations is not made within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt during the delayed period shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The court costs of the first instance are RMB 591,800, and the litigation preservation fee is RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 596,800, to be borne by Shenghuo Mining Company.

Shenghuo Mining Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court on the following grounds: (A) The judgment of first instance erred in holding that this case did not constitute a change of circumstances. 1. The policy change was the core reason for the inability to obtain a mining right license. After Shenghuo Mining Company and Dazong Company signed the "Cooperative Operating Contract" on July 28, 2007, the exploration rights for three coal resources were transferred to Huaibei Zongsheng Company and Suzhou Zongsheng Company. In the ensuing years, the mining right license was not successfully obtained precisely because Zong Chengle consistently failed to fulfill his promise to handle the mining right license and corresponding mine construction procedures. Although the "Guiding Opinions" only used the expression that "in principle, no new coal mine projects will be constructed in the eastern region for some time to come," in practice, the construction of new coal mine projects had become definitively impossible. It was precisely because of the "Guiding Opinions" that obtaining a mining right license became impossible; based on this, no third party would be willing to acquire the exploration rights. If the "Guiding Opinions" had already existed at the time of signing the "Equity Transfer Agreement," Shenghuo Mining Company would naturally not have signed the "Equity Transfer Agreement." Therefore, it was precisely the issuance of the "Guiding Opinions" that changed the objective circumstances on which the "Equity Transfer Agreement" relied. 2. The circumstances that occurred in this case were not commercial risks and were unforeseeable. "Inability to transfer" was not the risk that arose in this case; the "Guiding Opinions" were the risk. The "Equity Transfer Agreement" effectively allowed Shenghuo Mining Company to obtain full control of the exploration rights for the three coal resources through the transfer of equity. Without the issuance of the "Guiding Opinions," Shenghuo Mining Company could either handle the mining right license itself, cooperate with other parties, or transfer the rights again. Even if no third party was willing to acquire the exploration rights to the three coal resources through the transfer of equity, Shenghuo Mining Company could still complete the development of the three coal resources on its own. However, precisely because of the issuance of the "Guiding Opinions," the exploration right certificates for the three coal resources had lost all value; Shenghuo Mining Company could neither develop the three coal resources on its own, nor cooperate with other parties, nor transfer them again. The contractual purpose of Shenghuo Mining Company—to obtain the exploration right certificates for the three coal resources through the transfer of equity and subsequently complete the mine construction and realize production—could no longer be achieved. 3. The exploration right certificates for the three coal resources were not void, expired, or invalid. The judgment of first instance held that Article 4 of the "Equity Transfer Agreement" stipulated that regardless of whether the exploration licenses or mining licenses related to the three coal resources owned by the two companies were void, expired, or invalid, Shenghuo Mining Company would unconditionally perform all terms of this agreement. Therefore, it could be determined that Shenghuo Mining Company could foresee possible risks. The judgment of first instance erred in applying this provision and concluding that Shenghuo Mining Company could foresee possible risks. The meaning of "expiry or invalidity" of the exploration right certificates for the three coal resources is not directly defined in current law. According to relevant regulations, it should be understood as the expiration and invalidation of the exploration right certificate due to failure to renew after its term. The "Guiding Opinions" are unrelated to the above situation; the issuance of the "Guiding Opinions" did not cause the exploration right certificates for the three coal resources to become void, expired, or invalid. Therefore, the finding in the first instance judgment that Shenghuo Mining Company could foresee the risk of the issuance of the "Guiding Opinions" is also untenable. 4. The judgment of first instance erred in holding that the first installment of the equity transfer payment did not satisfy the principle of change of circumstances. The principle of change of circumstances should apply to the entire contract, and its application cannot be differentiated based on whether certain obligations are due or not. If it is determined to be a change of circumstances, the effect is to modify or rescind the contract. If the contract is rescinded, according to the performance status and the nature of the "Equity Transfer Agreement," the status quo ante can naturally be restored, and the first installment of the equity transfer payment should naturally also be restored. Furthermore, before the issuance of the "Guiding Opinions," the state had, in fact, been gradually tightening restrictions on new coal mine construction. Therefore, due to concerns about policy, Shenghuo Mining Company did not pay the first installment of the equity transfer payment before July 31, 2014. It is inconsistent with the facts for the first instance judgment to determine that the first installment of the equity transfer payment did not fall under the principle of change of circumstances based solely on the issuance date of the "Guiding Opinions." If the contract continues to be performed, it would be manifestly unfair to Shenghuo Mining Company. Due to the change of circumstances, the "Equity Transfer Agreement" should be rescinded, and Shenghuo Mining Company is no longer required to pay any amount to Dazong Company. (B) The judgment of first instance erred in holding that Dazong Company's act of capital contribution withdrawal did not affect the purpose of the equity transfer contract. Since the first instance judgment had already determined that the "Equity Transfer Agreement" was a legal relationship concerning the transfer of equity, not the transfer of exploration rights, Dazong Company's withdrawal of capital contribution must necessarily affect the purpose of the equity transfer contract. If there was a withdrawal of capital contribution, the equity itself was defective, and the subject matter of the sale, being the quality of the most important subject matter in a sales contract, was defective; Dazong Company should naturally bear corresponding liability for breach of contract. However, the first instance judgment did not adjudicate this fact. It also did not rule on Shenghuo Mining Company's application to request the accounting books and vouchers of Huaibei Zongsheng Company, but instead directly rendered a judgment without ascertaining the facts.

In summary, the judgment of first instance contained errors in both fact-finding and legal application. Shenghuo Mining Company's appeal requests: 1. to set aside the judgment of first instance; 2. to dismiss all claims of Dazong Company and Zong Xijin; 3. to have all litigation costs of this case borne by Dazong Company and Zong Xijin.

Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court on the following grounds: (A) The grounds for Dazong Company and Zong Xijin's lawsuit are untenable and their claims should be dismissed. 1. In this case, Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company merely promised to repay Dazong Company's creditor's rights with future real estate sales proceeds, not to repay them with all of their own property. Therefore, the content of the "Letter of Commitment" is clearly different in nature from a guarantee and does not constitute a guarantee. 2. There is no confusion of legal personality between Huaibei Real Estate Company, Guoyang Real Estate Company, and Shenghuo Mining Company, and Dazong Company and Zong Xijin did not adduce evidence to prove such confusion. 3. Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company never undertook joint and several liability. There are no words such as "joint and several" or similar expressions in the "Letter of Commitment." In this regard, the first instance judgment also adopted the same finding and did not recognize the nature of guarantee liability or joint and several liability that Dazong Company and Zong Xijin asserted in their complaint. Logically, their claims should have been directly dismissed. (B) The court of first instance ruled beyond the scope of the claims. Based on the foregoing reasons, Dazong Company and Zong Xijin's claim in their complaint was for "guarantee liability" and "joint and several liability," and they never claimed that the defendants should bear "joint repayment liability" "within the scope of the company's real estate sales proceeds." However, the court of first instance never indicated to the parties that it might render a judgment on a different type of liability, and yet it issued a judgment exceeding the scope of the claims, which is clearly erroneous. (C) The performance obligation specified in the first instance judgment is unclear and cannot serve as a basis for enforcement; it should be set aside. The "Letter of Commitment" constitutes a conditional assumption of debt: first, it is conditional on the limitation of the property used for debt repayment; second, it is conditional on the limitation of the repayment period. Therefore, before obtaining the real estate sales proceeds, Dazong Company cannot demand repayment of the creditor's rights. Since it is uncertain whether the real estate will be sold in the future, it is also uncertain when the condition for debt settlement will be fulfilled. Given that the obligation stipulated in the "Letter of Commitment" is a conditional debt, the debt is not due for settlement until the condition is satisfied. However, during the trial of first instance, it was not ascertained whether the condition for the performance of the debt in this case had been fulfilled, i.e., whether the "real estate sales proceeds" had been obtained. Because whether the real estate in this case had been sold was uncertain, it would inevitably shift to the enforcement judge the substantive determination of whether the future debt had been settled, which would seriously violate the principle of "separation of trial and enforcement" in civil procedure law. Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company's appeal requests: 1. to set aside items 1 and 2 of the first instance judgment; 2. to amend the judgment and dismiss the claims of Dazong Company and Zong Xijin; 3. to have all litigation costs of this case borne by Dazong Company and Zong Xijin.

Dazong Company and Zong Xijin argued in defense: (A) The "Equity Transfer Agreement" in this case is legally valid, and Shenghuo Mining Company should continue to perform it. 1. Shenghuo Mining Company's assertion that the "Equity Transfer Agreement" was a transfer of exploration rights has no factual basis. Dazong Company and Zong Xijin are not holders of exploration rights; what was transferred was merely company equity. The reference to transferring exploration rights in the liquidated damages promissory note is merely Shenghuo Mining Company's unilateral understanding. Shenghuo Mining Company failed to perform its contractual obligations and should bear liability for breach of contract. 2. After the "Equity Transfer Agreement" was signed, Shenghuo Mining Company had full control of the two companies and paid part of the liquidated damages. At the time Huaibei Zongsheng Company was established, Shenghuo Mining Company did not make any capital contribution. After Dazong Company made its capital contribution, part of the funds were used for business operations, which was certified by the seal of Li Xiufang, the legal representative of Huaibei Zongsheng Company. Since the legal representative of Shenghuo Mining Company is Li Xiufang's son, Shenghuo Mining Company should be presumed to have known this. If Shenghuo Mining Company believes that its expression of intent at the time of signing the "Equity Transfer Agreement" was not genuine, the statutory one-year exclusionary period has also expired. (B) The change in relevant national policies after the signing of the "Equity Transfer Agreement" does not meet the conditions for the principle of change of circumstances. The provision in Article 4, Paragraph 1 of the "Equity Transfer Agreement" is very clear, indicating that changes in national policies leading to the voiding or expiration of the exploration and mining licenses for the three coal resources were within the contemplation of both parties. Moreover, the agreement stipulates that even if such circumstances arise, Shenghuo Mining Company cannot request the rescission or modification of the agreement but must unconditionally perform the contract. As a mining enterprise, Shenghuo Mining Company should have even more foresight regarding the various risks that may arise in the industry, including those brought about by changes in natural conditions, social events, or national policies. In China's economic zoning, Anhui Province belongs to the central region, not the eastern region, and the "Guiding Opinions" do not apply to this case. Subsequently, Shenghuo Mining Company issued a promissory note and a letter of commitment and paid part of the liquidated damages, indicating that it was well aware of the terms of the "Equity Transfer Agreement." (C) Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company should bear joint repayment liability for Shenghuo Mining Company's debts within the scope of their real estate sales proceeds. The "Letter of Commitment" clearly states that they would prioritize repayment of Dazong Company's matured creditor's rights with their real estate sales proceeds. Although the first instance judgment ordering Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company to bear joint repayment liability is different from the joint and several liability claimed by Dazong Company, there is no substantive difference, and it does not constitute a judgment exceeding the scope of the claims. The argument by Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company that they bear a conditional payment obligation and that it is unclear whether the real estate has been sold, making enforcement impossible, is untenable. If the companies maliciously fail to sell the real estate, the court can auction their real estate to satisfy the debt. (D) There is absolutely no issue of Dazong Company withdrawing capital contribution from Huaibei Zongsheng Company. Shenghuo Mining Company had full control of the two companies and had already achieved the purpose of the contract. Its legal representative is the son of the legal representative of Huaibei Zongsheng Company and should have known whether the equity had any defects. Shenghuo Mining Company filed a separate lawsuit on this matter in the Suixian People's Court of Anhui Province, indicating that this issue can be resolved in a separate case and has no impact on this case.

During the second instance, Shenghuo Mining Company submitted four pieces of new evidence: The first piece of evidence is the "Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Further Strengthening Safety Production in Coal Mines" dated October 2, 2013, intended to prove that the three coal mines involved in this case could not be newly constructed and had no value. The second piece of evidence is the "Certificate of Filing and Approval for the Review and Confirmation of Mineral Resource Reserves in the Qilusunjing Coalfield Geological Survey Report of Suzhou City, Anhui Province," intended to prove that the coal mine is a coal and gas outburst mine. The third piece of evidence is the "Coal Exploration Report for the Qilusunjing Coalfield of Suzhou City, Anhui Province," intended to prove that this coal resource is a coal and gas outburst mine. The fourth piece of evidence is the "Certificate of Filing and Approval for the Review and Confirmation of Mineral Resource Reserves in the Zhangyoufang Coalfield Coal Exploration Report of the Huaibei Coalfield, Anhui Province," intended to prove that this coal resource is a coal and gas outburst mine. Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company, in their comments on the evidence, acknowledged the authenticity of the evidence and Shenghuo Mining Company's statements. Dazong Company and Zong Xijin, in their comments on the evidence, stated that they had no objection to the authenticity of the four pieces of evidence. Regarding the first piece of evidence, coal and gas outburst mines with capacities of 300,000 tons and 900,000 tons do not include the figures themselves and are not applicable to this case. They had no comments on the second and third pieces of evidence. The expression in the fourth piece of evidence is only an inference and cannot be taken as a conclusion. Dazong Company and Zong Xijin argued that the four pieces of evidence could not prove the occurrence of a change of circumstances. Even assuming that national policy reasons prevented expansion, the parties had already made clear provisions in the equity transfer agreement, had foreseen this, and the evidence could not achieve its purpose of proof.

Dazong Company and Zong Xijin submitted three pieces of new evidence: The first piece of evidence is the "Several Opinions of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council on Promoting the Rise of the Central Region" (Zhongfa [2006] No. 10), intended to prove that Anhui Province is not part of the eastern region in economic zoning. The second piece of evidence is the "Cooperative Operating Contract" dated July 28, 2007, intended to prove that both parties foresaw the risk of being unable to construct mines due to national policies. The third piece of evidence is a "Letter Concerning the Cooperation Situation" from Huaibei Mining (Group) Co., Ltd. to the Huaibei Municipal People's Government in 2013, intended to prove that Shenghuo Mining Company proposed the equity transfer based on its desire to cooperate with Huaibei Mining (Group) Co., Ltd. Shenghuo Mining Company, in its comments on the evidence, stated that it had no objection to the authenticity of the three pieces of evidence. However, the first piece of evidence was not issued specifically concerning mineral resources and is irrelevant to this case. The Anhui Provincial People's Government had already issued a notice on March 28, 2014, clarifying that coal and gas outburst mines cannot be newly constructed. The second piece of evidence was replaced by the 2013 equity transfer agreement, and the agreement itself stated that if a policy change occurred, the parties would share the costs equally. The third piece of evidence had already been submitted in the first instance, and citing it does not serve the purpose of proof, nor can it indicate which party proactively proposed the transfer. Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company, in their comments on the evidence, stated that they had objections to the authenticity of the first piece of evidence, as Anhui Province was treated as the eastern region, and newly constructed coal mines were not approved. The second piece of evidence indicates that the parties would equally share preliminary expenses; they recognized that if handled according to the 2007 agreement, there would be no need to pay RMB 650 million. They acknowledged the authenticity of the third piece of evidence, but because Anhui Province did not approve new mine construction, the mining license could not be obtained, resulting in a change of circumstances.

After the hearing, Dazong Company submitted a partial list of its investments in Huaibei Zongsheng Company along with related receipts, certificates, and other documents, totaling RMB 2,829,448. Shenghuo Mining Company, Huaibei Real Estate Company, and Guoyang Real Estate Company submitted written comments on the evidence: 1. Regarding the "Unified Invoice for Motor Vehicle Sales" and the "General Tax Payment Certificate of the People's Republic of China": The vehicle was not registered under Huaibei Zongsheng Company, nor was it ever used; the entire vehicle purchase process was controlled by Dazong Company. 2. Regarding the "Certificate," a copy of Yang Sucheng's ID card, and two rent payment vouchers: The payment vouchers show that Suzhou Zongsheng Company made the payment, and the payment date does not correspond to the lease period. 3. Regarding two surveying fee invoices: Huaibei Zongsheng Company never engaged in any specific business, so no surveying fees should have arisen. In summary, they did not accept Dazong Company's evidence, and Dazong Company could not prove that it had actually made investments in Huaibei Zongsheng Company.

With respect to the above evidence, this Court makes the following comprehensive determination: The first piece of evidence submitted by Shenghuo Mining Company, Dazong Company, and Zong Xijin respectively constitutes a normative document issued by the State Council, which this Court will use as a reference for determining the facts of this case in accordance with the law. The other three pieces of evidence submitted by Shenghuo Mining Company, since all parties have no objection to their authenticity, are admitted by this Court. The second and third pieces of evidence submitted by Dazong Company and Zong Xijin as new evidence were already submitted and cross-examined during the first instance; they are not new evidence. Regarding the partial list of Dazong Company's investments in Huaibei Zongsheng Company and the receipts, certificates, and other documents submitted by Dazong Company, since Shenghuo Mining Company, Huaibei Real Estate Company, and Guoyang Real Estate Company do not recognize them, and their relevance to this case cannot be confirmed, this Court does not admit this evidence in this case.

Other facts found in the second instance are consistent with those found in the first instance.

This Court holds that the issues in dispute in this case are: (A) Whether the first instance judgment erred in finding that the first installment of the equity transfer payment did not satisfy the principle of change of circumstances; (B) Whether the first instance judgment erred in finding that the "Equity Transfer Agreement" was valid and whether the agreement should continue to be performed; (C) Whether the first instance judgment erred in ordering Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company to bear joint repayment liability for Shenghuo Mining Company's debts within the scope of real estate sales proceeds; (D) If there was a withdrawal of capital contribution, whether it affects the trial of this case.

(A) Regarding the issue of whether the first instance judgment erred in finding that the first installment of the transfer payment did not satisfy the principle of change of circumstances.

Article 26 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "After the formation of a contract, if the objective circumstances have undergone a significant change that was unforeseeable at the time of entering into the contract, not attributable to force majeure, and does not constitute a commercial risk, and the performance of the contract would be manifestly unfair to one party or the purpose of the contract cannot be achieved, the party requesting the court to modify or rescind the contract shall, in accordance with the principle of fairness and in light of the actual circumstances of the case, determine whether to modify or rescind the contract." Whether a situation constitutes a so-called change of circumstances or a commercial risk requires reference to the contract's terms and analysis based on aspects such as foreseeability, imputability, and consequences. In this case, Huaibei Zongsheng Company was established in 2007. Applications for mining right procedures or project approval for the three coal resources involved had been ongoing until the "Guiding Opinions" on October 12, 2014, without approval. Furthermore, the "Guiding Opinions" only stated that, in principle, no new coal mine projects would be constructed in the eastern region for some time to come, and whether Anhui Province fell within the eastern region as defined by the "Guiding Opinions" required further demonstration. Therefore, policy reasons were not the only cause for the failure to obtain approval for the cooperative development project.

Article 4 of the Equity Transfer Agreement involved in this case stipulates that regardless of whether the exploration licenses or mining licenses related to the three coal resources owned by Huaibei Zongsheng Company and Suzhou Zongsheng Company are revoked, expired, or invalidated, Shenghuo Mining Company shall unconditionally perform all terms of this Agreement. Article 2 stipulates that before July 31, 2014, Shenghuo Mining Company shall pay the first installment of the equity transfer price to Dazong Company. Shenghuo Mining Company has no objection to this, and when it failed to pay the first installment on time, it issued an IOU for RMB 20,000,000 in liquidated damages to Dazong Company and actually paid RMB 10,000,000. Since the Guiding Opinions were issued on October 12, 2014, the first-instance judgment's finding that the payment of this first installment does not satisfy the principle of change of circumstances is supported by facts. Shenghuo Mining Company's defense that it should not be obligated to pay the first installment of the equity transfer price based on the principle of change of circumstances is not accepted by this Court.

(2) Whether the first-instance judgment correctly found the equity transfer agreement valid and whether the agreement should be further performed

The Equity Transfer Agreement signed on March 24, 2013, by Dazong Company, Zong Xijin, and Shenghuo Mining Company represented the true intent of the parties and did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations. The first-instance judgment's determination that the Agreement was legally valid and effective is proper. In the Agreement, the parties stipulated that Dazong Company and Zong Xijin would transfer all of their lawfully held 44% equity interests in Suzhou Zongsheng Company and Huaibei Zongsheng Company to Shenghuo Mining Company, and Shenghuo Mining Company would pay the transfer price. The exploration license and mining license for the three coal resources have always remained in the names of the two target companies, and there was no issue of change or approval. After the Equity Transfer Agreement was signed, Shenghuo Mining Company actually took control of the two target companies, thereby achieving the purpose of the contract. Therefore, the legal relationship between the parties was one of equity transfer. Shenghuo Mining Company's assertion that this case involved a transfer of exploration rights and that the contract was not effective due to lack of approval is not supported by this Court.

Given that the claims of Dazong Company and Zong Xijin in the first instance were only for an order directing Shenghuo Mining Company to pay the first installment of the equity transfer price and liquidated damages, and did not include a request for further performance of the Agreement, although the first-instance judgment contains statements such as "Because the equity transfer agreement is legally valid and effective, the claim of Dazong Company and Zong Xijin that Shenghuo Mining Company should continue to perform and pay the overdue first installment of RMB 100,000,000 and the unpaid liquidated damages of RMB 10,000,000 is supported by this Court," these statements are still based on the claim of Dazong Company and Zong Xijin for payment of the first installment and liquidated damages. Whether the Equity Transfer Agreement should be further performed requires active assertion by the parties. Shenghuo Mining Company argues that this case satisfies the principle of change of circumstances and the Agreement should not be further performed. However, because the payment of the first installment does not satisfy the principle of change of circumstances, Shenghuo Mining Company's defense against the payment of the first installment cannot stand. As to whether the Equity Transfer Agreement should be further performed or rescinded, since Dazong Company and Zong Xijin did not raise this claim in the first instance, and Shenghuo Mining Company did not file a counterclaim, this matter is beyond the scope of this Court's review in the second instance, and this Court will not adjudicate it.

(3) Whether the first-instance judgment erred in ordering Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company to bear joint repayment liability for Shenghuo Mining Company's debts to the extent of their real estate sales proceeds.

In this case, Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company issued a Letter of Commitment to Dazong Company, promising to first use real estate sales proceeds to repay Dazong Company's due claims in accordance with the contract, and affixed their official seals in the guarantor section. This Court holds that the Letter of Commitment represented the true intent of Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company, and their commitment does not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations. They should perform their corresponding obligations in accordance with the commitment. The essence of Dazong Company's lawsuit against Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company is to request the two real estate companies to assume corresponding legal responsibilities based on the commitment letter. After review, the first-instance court found that Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company did not constitute joint and several guarantor liability but should bear joint repayment liability for Shenghuo Mining Company's debts to the extent of their real estate sales proceeds. The first-instance judgment did not substantially increase their civil liability, and this Court affirms this. Whether the properties of Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company have been sold is recorded by relevant authorities and documented by tax authorities; there is no issue of uncertainty or impossibility of enforcement. The claims of Huaibei Real Estate Company and Guoyang Real Estate Company lack factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support them.

(4) Whether the existence of capital contribution evasion, if any, affects the adjudication of this case.

The first-instance judgment held that if Dazong Company had evaded capital contributions to Huaibei Zongsheng Company, Huaibei Zongsheng Company would have the right to demand that the shareholder make up the contribution. Shenghuo Mining Company submitted evidence in the second instance to prove that it had filed a lawsuit against Dazong Company for capital contribution evasion with the Sui County People's Court of Anhui Province, demonstrating that it still has a remedy channel. Therefore, Shenghuo Mining Company's request to stay the proceedings in this case has no legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, the appeals of Shenghuo Mining Company, Huaibei Real Estate Company, and Guoyang Real Estate Company are without merit. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and it should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 591,800 shall be jointly borne by the appellants, Huaibei Shenghuo Mining Co., Ltd., Huaibei Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Guoyang Shenghuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
